'''Morio Obata''' (小畠 守生, ''Obata Morio''; June 5, 1926 – December 21, 2006) was a Japanese [[mathematician]] who contributed to [[geometry]] and [[Mathematical analysis|analysis]].

== Life and career ==
Obata was born on June 5, 1926, in [[Busan]], [[Korea under Japanese rule|Korea, Empire of Japan]].<ref name="marquis">{{cite book |title=Who's Who in the World, 1987-1988 |publisher=[[Marquis Who's Who]] |date=December 1986 |page=758 }}</ref>

Obata obtained a [[bachelor of science]] degree from the Fifth College at [[Kumamoto University]] in 1947<ref name="marquis"/> and subsequently studied under the guidance of [[Kentaro Yano (mathematician)|Kentaro Yano]] at the [[University of Tokyo]], who was frequently away working at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]] and other institutions. A chance meeting with [[Shizuo Kakutani]] in 1947 influenced Obata's decision to pursue [[differential geometry]] as his field of research, as Kakutani remarked that if he were younger and just starting his mathematical career, he would be studying it. Obata obtained a [[master of science]] degree from the University of Tokyo in 1950.<ref name="marquis"/> In 1951, he joined the [[Tokyo Metropolitan University]] and published joint papers with his friend Shigeru Ishihara on [[affine connection]]s and [[conformal transformation]]s from 1953 to 1955.<ref name="Nagano"/> In 1956, he established that an irreducible noncompact [[Kähler manifold]] admits [[isometries]] which are not [[holomorphic]] only if the [[holonomy group]] is the [[symplectic group]] <math>\text{Sp}(n)</math>.<ref name="Nagano">{{cite conference | last=Nagano | first=Tadashi | last2=Omori | first2=Hideki | last3=Maeda | first3=Yoshiaki | last4=Kanai | first4=Masahiko | title=Geometry and its Applications; In Honor of Morio Obata: Proceedings of the Workshop | publisher=World Scientific | date=1993 | isbn=978-981-02-1205-6 | doi=10.1142/9789814536479 | url=http://www.worldscientific.com/doi/abs/10.1142/9789814536479 | access-date=2025-07-22| url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Obata |first=Morio |title=Affine transformations in an almost complex manifold with a natural affine connection |journal=[[Mathematical Society of Japan|Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan]] |volume=8 |issue=4 |date=October 1956 |pages=345–362}}</ref> Obata's [[dissertation]] was on affine connections on [[manifolds]] with [[Almost complex manifold|almost complex]], [[Quaternionic manifold#Almost quaternionic structure|almost quaternion]], and [[Hermitian manifold|almost Hermitian structure]].<ref>{{cite journal
|last=Obata
|first=Morio
|title=Affine connections on manifolds with almost complex, quaternion or Hermitian structure
|journal=Japanese Journal of Mathematics: Transactions and Abstracts
|publisher=The Mathematical Society of Japan
|volume=26
|pages=43–77
|year=1956
|doi=10.4099/JJM1924.26.0_43
|doi-access=free
}}</ref> He earned his [[doctorate]] in 1958.<ref name="marquis"/>

From 1958 to 1961, he worked as a visiting mathematician and research [[assistant professor]] at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]]<ref>{{cite web |last=Leetaru |first=Kalev |title=UIHistories Project: A History of the University of Illinois - Board of Trustees Minutes 1962 |url=https://uihistories.library.illinois.edu/cgi-bin/rview_browsepdf?REPOSID=8&ID=8125&pagenum=458 |website=UIHistories Project |publisher=[[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign University Library]] |page=459 |access-date=2025-07-22 |quote=OBATA, MORIO, Research Assistant Professor of Mathematics, February 1-March 20, 1961, $1,000 (3-6-61).}}</ref><ref name="marquis"/><ref name="Nagano"/> until he joined Tokyo Metropolitan University staff as an [[associate professor]].<ref name="marquis"/> In 1963, he participated in [[fundraising]] efforts for mathematical research and worked with [[Takeo Fujisawa]] (then vice-president of [[Honda|Honda Motor Company]]) to secure funding for the mathematical community through the Sakkokai foundation.<ref name="Nagano"/> Obata was made a [[full professor]] of mathematics in 1966.<ref name="marquis"/> After leaving Tokyo Metropolitan University in 1978, Obata moved to [[Keio University]], where he supervised a number of geometry graduate students. In 1987, Obata established the [[Geometry Prize]] of the [[Mathematical Society of Japan]], which is awarded to geometers for achievements, contributions, or guidance to younger researchers. By 1991, the prize had been awarded to ten geometers.<ref name="Nagano"/> He retired from Keio University in 1991 at the age of 65; a [[Academic conference|workshop]] celebrating his contributions to geometry and global analysis was held in his honor from November 19 to 21 of the same year.<ref name="Nagano"/>

Obata died on December 21, 2006, at the age of 80. He was a member of the [[American Mathematical Society]] for 47 years.<ref>{{cite journal|url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/200704/inside-web.pdf|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=54|number=4|page=544|title=Deaths of AMS Members}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
*Obata, Morio. "The conjectures on conformal transformations of Riemannian manifolds." (1971): 265–270.
*Obata, Morio. "Certain conditions for a Riemannian manifold to be isometric with a sphere Dedicated to Professor Kentaro Yano on his fiftieth birthday." ''Journal of the Mathematical Society of Japan'' 14.3 (1962): 333–340.
*Obata, Morio. "Affine connections on manifolds with almost complex, quaternion or Hermitian structure." Japanese journal of mathematics: transactions and abstracts. Vol. 26. [[Mathematical Society of Japan|The Mathematical Society of Japan]], 1956.
*Obata, Morio. "Conformal transformations of Riemannian manifolds." ''[[Journal of Differential Geometry]]'' 4.3 (1970): 311–333.
*Obata, Morio. "The Gauss map of immersions of Riemannian manifolds in spaces of constant curvature." ''Journal of Differential Geometry'' 2.2 (1968): 217–223.
